key_insight: In low-dimensional pnictogen chalcohalides, the most stable surface facets can still shift band edges by up to 0.8 eV, making surface orientation a hidden driver of solar-cell performance.
engineering_relevance: Device design for MChX photovoltaics should account for facet-dependent band alignment at charge-selective contacts, because mixed surface orientations can significantly reduce open-circuit voltage.
method: First-principles calculations across the MChX family
Exhaustive sampling of crystal orientations, including low-symmetry facets
evidence_signal: Across eight compounds, the (011) and (010) surfaces were found to be the most stable terminations, with formation energies differing by only about 0.01–0.03 J m^-2 but band-edge shifts reaching 0.8 eV and Voc losses up to 0.6 V in simulation.
watch_item: The results are strongly facet- and interface-dependent, so real devices may vary with surface reconstruction, defects, and contact chemistry beyond the idealized model.
paper_title: Surface Physics of Low-Dimensional Pnictogen Chalcohalides and Its Impact on Photovoltaic Technologies
